name: F. A. Abel
summary: English munitions chemist known for stabilizing guncotton and co-inventing cordite.

name: Seymour H. Mauskopf
summary: Historian of chemistry and author of the source document.

name: Andrew Noble
summary: Polymath in gunnery and munitions who collaborated with Abel.

name: James Dewar
summary: Chemist who collaborated with Abel on cordite.

name: Wilhelm Von Lenk
summary: Austrian artillery officer who developed an early guncotton production method.

name: Paul Vieille
summary: French chemist who developed Poudre B smokeless powder.

name: Royal College of Chemistry
summary: London chemistry school where Abel was a charter student.

name: St. Bartholomew's Hospital
summary: London hospital where Abel served as Demonstrator of Chemistry.

name: Royal Military Academy, Woolwich
summary: Military academy where Abel was Lecturer in Chemistry.

name: War Office
summary: British government department employing Abel as Chemist.

name: Woolwich Arsenal
summary: Military facility where Abel moved and conducted research.

name: guncotton
summary: Highly nitrated form of cellulose used as an explosive.

name: cordite
summary: Smokeless military propellant devised by Abel and Dewar.

name: gunpowder
summary: Traditional military propellant mixture of saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal.
